selection_rules: Every Indigenous and Oceanic record names a community scope; no record stands for a continent, race, language family, or all Indigenous peoples.
Use community-led, community-authorized, primary, or established regionally grounded scholarship; published availability never implies permission to extract restricted or ceremonial knowledge.
Record speaker, community, language, genre/performance, audience, place, authority to share, researcher/editor, archive, consent, and translation limits where sources expose them.
Central Asian, Southeast Asian, Buddhist, Islamic, Persianate, Chinese, Russian/Soviet, national, nomadic, and Indigenous scopes remain distinct even when histories overlap.
Māori, Kānaka Maoli, Samoan, Tongan, iTaukei, Ni-Vanuatu, CHamoru, and other Oceanic identities are never collapsed into one Pacific relational worldview.
No customary, ceremonial, spiritual, land, sovereignty, legal, gender, chiefly, nationalist, ecological, decolonial, or community claim becomes Factorium guidance.
